topic: Advanced Python: Iterators, Generators, and Decorators
learningObjectives: Explain how iterators and generators control data iteration.
Use generator functions to process values lazily.
Understand how decorators modify or extend function behavior.

activities.title: Iterator Map
activities.instruction: Explore how Python obtains values from an iterable.

content.concept: An iterator implements the iteration protocol and provides values one at a time. The iter() function obtains an iterator and next() retrieves the next value.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: An object that can provide its members one at a time, such as a list.
Creates an iterator from an iterable.
Object that produces successive values through __next__().
Requests the next value from an iterator.
Exception raised when the iterator has no more values.

activities.title: Generator Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore how yield turns a function into a generator function.

content.concept: A function containing yield becomes a generator function. Calling it returns a generator, and each next() call resumes execution until the next yield.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Continues while the limit has not been reached.
Produces the current value and pauses execution.
Updates the value before the next iteration.
Creates a generator object; the function body does not run to completion immediately.

activities.title: Lazy Evaluation Explorer
activities.instruction: Adjust the number of values requested from a generator.

content.concept: Generators produce values on demand. They can process large or potentially unbounded sequences without creating all values in memory at once.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Decorator Builder
activities.instruction: Assemble the components of a simple function decorator.

content.concept: A decorator is a callable that takes a function and returns a wrapped function, allowing behavior to be added around the original call.
